misconceptions.description: Believing that repeating buzzwords to game applicant tracking systems improves a resume
misconceptions.trigger: learner accepts AI advice to repeat a keyword regardless of whether it reflects real skill
misconceptions.feedback: Stuffed keywords read as spam to the human reviewer. Use terms from the posting that name skills you actually have.

misconceptions.description: Treating AI feedback as more authoritative than the assignment's own stated requirements
misconceptions.trigger: learner follows AI advice that conflicts with the posting or rubric
misconceptions.feedback: When AI feedback conflicts with the stated requirements, the requirements win. Reject advice that breaks the brief.

misconceptions.description: Overcorrecting by rejecting every AI suggestion, including legitimate, truthful improvements
misconceptions.trigger: learner discards a valid edit (like trimming an outdated line) because it came from AI
misconceptions.feedback: Reject fabrication, not all feedback. Keep truthful, relevant improvements and log why you kept them.

misconceptions.description: Judging AI feedback by how confident or advanced it sounds rather than whether the claim is defensible
misconceptions.trigger: learner accepts a suggestion because the tool stated it assertively or with fancy wording
misconceptions.feedback: Apply the defensibility test: could you stand behind the resulting claim in an interview? If not, reject it.
